issues.title: Tighten weighted hard-stops budgets from observed spend (post-SYMPH-955 re-baseline)
issues.description:
**Problem**

SYMPH-955 flips the hard-stops budget gate to the weighted cost-equivalent unit and re-baselines every `max_tokens_per_unit` by a **conservative ×6** (the max output weight, OpenAI), guaranteeing the weighted gate fires no earlier than the old billable gate for any token mix/provider. ×6 is a deliberate upper bound chosen because no weighted-unit spend data existed at flip time (the measure did not exist until SYMPH-955 landed). For non-output-heavy units it loosens the effective ceiling up to ~6×, so it should be tightened once real data exists (measure-before-caps).

**Acceptance criteria**

* Collect a measurement window of weighted-unit spend per stage (subscription/credit weighted_tokens; api_token usd) from production runs after SYMPH-955 deploys.
* Derive per-config `max_tokens_per_unit` (and the default) from observed weighted distributions (e.g. p95 of real weighted spend + grace), replacing the flat ×6 bound. Document the observed→new mapping; operator sign-off.
* Consider whether thresholds should become provider-aware (Claude 5× vs OpenAI 6×) instead of a single provider-agnostic number — decide from the data, do not assume.

**Source refs**

* SYMPH-955 (parent): introduced the weighted unit + ×6 conservative re-baseline; mapping in `docs/DEV_GUIDE.md`.
* `src/policy/hard-stops.ts` (weighted gate), `src/policy/pricing.ts` (resolver), crucible `lane_workers/pricing.ts` (shared unit).
* Surfaced by the SYMPH-955 session-orchestrator run (decorrelated review + operator decision: direct flip now, tighten later).

comments.body:
**Adversarial re-review — VALIDATED, and arguably under-prioritized (tried to kill it; couldn't).**

- Not just the deprecating in-process gate: `src/stage-execution/job-spec.ts` forwards `budget.maxTokens = hardStops.maxTokensPerUnit` to the crabrunner **lanes**, so the ×6 value governs lane-side (MOB-589) enforcement too.
- **Elevated risk:** SYMPH-955 dropped the dollar-budget + premium-spend-near-ceiling for subscription/credit lanes (operator decision), so the weighted-token ceiling is now the **sole token-cost budget gate** for the common case. A conservative ×6 lets a non-output-heavy subscription unit burn up to ~6× the intended budget before that sole gate fires (iteration/no-progress/stall caps still bound progress, but not cost). So tightening is real risk-reduction, not speculative optimization.
- **Actionable now:** the data exists — the session-orchestrator usage ledger records per-stage weighted/usd spend; derive per-config thresholds from the observed weighted distribution (e.g. p95 + grace). Keep.

issues.title: Spec-fidelity deviation-capture: Opus judge as a shared crabrunner lane (measure-only v1)
issues.description:
## Problem

The review lanes judge the diff in a vacuum. The crucible council prompt (`session-orchestrator/scripts/lib/review-prompt.mjs`) and symphony's reviewer prompt are anchored to "review exactly this diff," with the P1/P2 gate scoped to defects *introduced by this diff*. Under-delivery is an absence (no `file:line`, not "introduced by this diff") that the rubric routes to Track or drops — so a diff can under-deliver against the spec while the code that is present "works," and every reviewer passes it.

Symphony shipped a spec-fidelity judge (SYMPH-343) but it is dormant (`enabled:false`, in no shipped workflow), anchored only to tagged AC bullets, and runs on the local LLM (two weeks of operation: not capable of this judgment). Crucible's council has no spec-fidelity gate at all. So in production, nothing audits spec fidelity.

## Approach (measure-only v1)

A dedicated spec-fidelity judge on **Opus**, in **parallel** with the council, off the frozen diff, authored **once** as a lane in the crucible session-orchestrator substrate and consumed by both systems (DRY). It emits per-plan-item records classified `delivered` / `mechanism-deviation` / `explained-deferral` / `silent-drop` (+confidence +evidence). **Report-only.** v1 **gathers** records; the reconciliation layer (identity/projection/planner-feed/Linear summary) is **v1b**, designed from the v1 records.

This is an instance of **SYMPH-949**: once the judge runs on Opus it stops being a "local-model gate that stays in-process" and becomes a model-execution lane.

## Acceptance criteria (v1)

* check: A dedicated Opus spec-fidelity judge runs in parallel with the council off the frozen diff (not sequenced after review exit), in both symphony and crucible.
* check: The judge emits a structured per-plan-item record (`delivered`/`mechanism-deviation`/`explained-deferral`/`silent-drop` + confidence + evidence), written append-only to the durable sink.
* check: `explained-deferral` requires a rationale verifiable against diff+AC; rationale presence alone never downgrades a `silent-drop`.
* check: The judge's new evidence inputs (plan narrative, PR body, commits) are fenced as untrusted (named boundary tags + trust note + `prompt-fence` extension).
* check: Scope is AC-satisfaction + deviation capture only — not a second defect-hunter; non-AC bugs stay the council's job.
* check: Report-only; nothing blocks merge. Enforcement is a later per-bucket flip gated on a calibration window.

## Sub-issues

* [MOB / Crucible] Shared judge lane in the crucible substrate (prompt + record schema + classifier + Opus routing).
* [SYMPH] Symphony integration: retire the in-process local-LLM judge, dispatch the lane via the review group, extend evidence, amend SYMPH-949's in-process inventory.

## v1b (deferred — designed from v1 records)

Stable cross-round identity (needs `ac-gate`/SYMPH-354 enabled or a fallback id), latest-per-item projection, merge-time planner-feed contract, Linear projection summary.

## Open (resolve before planning)

* Plan-item identity anchor: `ac-gate` (SYMPH-354) is dormant, so AC tags are sparse — enable it as a dependency or specify a fallback id.
* Calibration ground-truth label source + falsifiable enforcement-flip threshold (else report-only has no exit criterion and Opus's competence at judging self-serving rationales stays unvalidated).

## Source

Brief: `docs/plans/2026-06-29-001-feat-spec-fidelity-deviation-capture-plan.md` (also published to Linear Docs). Surfaced in a brainstorm + ce-doc-review session 2026-06-29. Relates SYMPH-949, SYMPH-343, SYMPH-960. Code refs: `src/agent/spec-fidelity.ts`, `src/orchestrator/runtime-host.ts:1072`, `src/orchestrator/core.ts:4644`, `src/config/defaults.ts:251`, `src/review/spine/crabbox-spine-client.ts:28`, `src/tracker/ticket-feature.ts:866`, `session-orchestrator/scripts/lib/review-prompt.mjs`.

comments.body:
**Design correction (operator, 2026-06-29): the judge runs ADJACENT, not in-cycle.**

The council enforces one lane per model family per cycle (`resolveCouncilLanes` family-level decorrelation), and Opus is already the council's finder/judge — so an in-cycle Opus spec-fidelity lane would collide. The judge isn't a council reviewer anyway (different question, own rubric/schema, excluded from the council verdict), so it is dispatched as its **own adjacent cycle** parallel to the council off the same frozen diff, consuming no council model-family slot. Fleet has capacity for the concurrent Opus lane.

Plan changes: R5 reworded; new KTD7 (adjacency / no shared model slot); **U2** (crucible MOB-610) now emits a standalone `judge-spec-fidelity` stage *outside* `resolveCouncilLanes`/`reviewer_entries`; **U5** (symphony SYMPH-971) now dispatches a *separate* adjacent crabrunner job, not a lane in the council job-group. Doc resynced.

**Plan enriched to implementation-ready (ce-plan, 2026-06-29).** Doc resynced. Product Contract unchanged; added Planning Contract (6 KTDs), 6 Implementation Units, Verification Contract, Definition of Done.

**U-ID → ticket mapping:**
- **MOB-610 (crucible):** U1 (judge prompt builder + per-item record schema + untrusted-input fencing), U2 (wire the sibling non-finder Opus lane into council-flow).
- **SYMPH-971 (symphony-ts):** U3 (retire the in-process local-LLM judge; keep journal kind / merge gate / status), U4 (config + `spec_fidelity.enabled:true` workflow + amend SYMPH-949 inventory), U5 (dispatch the lane + assemble plan-narrative/PR-body evidence), U6 (collect the artifact → write `non_gating` records, report-only).

**Key seam decisions:** report-only = the existing `recordSpecFidelityNonGating` writer (so the existing `hasCurrentSpecFidelityRework` merge gate never fires; enforcement later = a writer flip); commit status omitted in v1; the `spec_fidelity` journal kind + merge gate are reused, not rebuilt. Sequencing: crucible U1→U2 first (artifact contract), then symphony U4→U5→U6 (U3 independent).

**Open-question resolutions (operator, 2026-06-29) — both now baked into the brief / Linear Doc.**

**1. Plan-item identity → enable `ac-gate` as a dependency.** AC tags are the identity anchor (R10, v1b); no fallback id is pursued. Enabling `ac-gate` (SYMPH-354) in the symphony workflow + verifying it produces/validates the tagged AC is a prerequisite of v1b, tracked as an AC on SYMPH-971.

**2. Calibration → collapse the gating distinction; calibrate only the checkable question.** After a critical re-review, the original "calibrate the explained-vs-silent distinction" was scrapped (the consumer-action label is circular, absence ≠ false-positive, and a disagreement-triage filter points *away* from the both-models-fooled gaming case). Resolution:
- Gating keys on **AC-met** (`delivered` + `mechanism-deviation`) vs **AC-unmet** (`explained-deferral` + `silent-drop`). The explained/silent split is **telemetry annotation, never a gating lever** — which designs the gaming vector out (a rationale labels the follow-up, it never excuses an unmet AC) and removes the un-calibratable rationale-soundness question.
- Calibrate only AC-satisfaction (met vs unmet) via independent re-read (operator and/or a decorrelated second strong model; cross-model disagreement = the audit queue). Downstream-outcome correlation is a supporting/biased signal, not the primary label.
- The eventual AC-unmet gate is characterized by false-block rate + recall (not precision alone), thresholds from observed data; a long report-only phase is an accepted state if AC-unmet is rare.

Affected requirements: R9a (reframed to annotation), R16 (AC-met-vs-unmet enforcement + calibration metric), AE2 (explained-deferral is AC-unmet under enforcement). Outstanding "resolve before planning" questions: none.

issues.title: Retire symphony inline Track-finding filer once the relay is authoritative
issues.description:
## Context

Track-finding → Linear filing is being unified onto a single Crucible-owned **ledger-driven relay** (MOB-604) that drains `Track` rows from the shared review-quality ledger, dedups on the `[track:<fp>]` marker, renders `Proposed by: <model>`, and writes the Linear join back onto the row. This replaces symphony's in-process inline filer.

Decision and full rationale: MOB-604 + `docs/plans/2026-06-29-002-feat-track-filing-ledger-relay-plan.md`.

Blocked by: **MOB-604** (the relay + shared ledger contract must exist and pass its shadow window first).

## Why still real

symphony-ts files Track findings inline at review→merge closeout via:

* `src/orchestrator/core.ts` → `fileTrackFindingsBestEffort` (closeout call site)
* `src/orchestrator/runtime-host.ts` → `fileTrackFindingsBestEffort` (the `TrackFindingFiler` adapter, `LinearTrackerClient.createTrackFindingIssue`)
* `src/orchestrator/track-finding-filing.ts` (pure formatting/selection/reconcile/journal-metadata)
* `src/review/review-track-findings.ts` (`computeTrackFiling` / `resolveTrackFindingFilings`)
* `src/tracker/linear-client.ts` → `createTrackFindingIssue`

Once the relay is authoritative, this inline path is redundant and would double-file (the relay dedups on the same marker, so it is not a correctness hazard during shadow, but it is wasted work and a second drifting surface).

symphony already appends `raised_by` to the ledger row via `src/review/spine/review-aggregator.ts` (`captureLedger`) → `src/review/spine/review-quality-ledger-client.ts`, so the relay has the attribution it needs with no symphony change on the capture side.

## Acceptance criteria

* During the MOB-604 **shadow window**, symphony keeps filing inline; the relay runs compute-only and the two are compared. No behavior change to symphony in this phase.
* On shadow-window exit (criteria defined in MOB-604), retire the symphony inline filer: remove/disable `fileTrackFindingsBestEffort` filing, the `TrackFindingFiler` injection, and the now-dead `track-finding-filing.ts` formatting/journal path — leaving the relay as the sole filer.
* The `track_finding_filing` run-journal kind and its dedup logic are removed or repurposed (no longer needed once the relay owns idempotency via the ledger + marker).
* The gate's `unfiled → warning` escalation (`src/review/headless-council-gate.ts:6294`) is repointed or removed: with the relay, "unfiled at closeout" is the normal queued state, so the inline warning would become noise. The assurance moves to the relay's lag signal (MOB-604).
* No filing gap at any point: inline filer is removed only after the relay is authoritative.
* Tests updated: remove/adjust the SYMPH-760/763 inline-filer tests; assert the closeout no longer files inline and that `raised_by` is present on the emitted ledger row.

## Verification

* `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build` (symphony-ts gates).
* Confirm via a fixture closeout that no inline Linear write occurs and the ledger row carries `raised_by` for the relay to consume.

* `src/orchestrator/runtime-host.ts` (`fileTrackFindingsBestEffort` adapter, ~2063-2168; injection ~1224)
* `src/orchestrator/track-finding-filing.ts`
* `src/review/review-track-findings.ts`, `src/review/headless-council-gate.ts` (~6294, ~6616)
* `src/tracker/linear-client.ts` (`createTrackFindingIssue`)
* Related: MOB-604 (relay + contract), SYMPH-760, SYMPH-763

issues.title: Retest SYMPH-962 Phase-A if transcript-only planner decisions appear
issues.description:
## Context

SYMPH-962 Phase-A measured whether structured post-session closeout capture has marginal planner value over the current session-time Linear surfaces. The ratified 2026-06-29 verdict was **NO-BUILD**: discovery totals were D=19, T=0, F=0, F*=0, and no qualifying transcript-only planner flip survived the Rev 2 decision rule.

This issue preserves the conditional re-test trigger required by the Phase-A gate. It is not Phase-B build work and should stay parked until one of the trigger conditions is observed.

## Why still real

The NO-BUILD verdict depends on today's observed surface coverage: session-time issue bodies, comments, native relations, and live planner comment/edge enrichment captured the durable planner-relevant decisions in the measured discovery sessions. If that coverage regresses, or if future discovery sessions expose clean planner-relevant decisions that remain transcript-only, the marginal-value measurement should be rerun before permanently treating closeout capture as unnecessary.

## Acceptance criteria

* Retest is only started when at least one trigger is observed:
  * a future discovery session contains a clean/explicit planner-relevant decision not captured by session-time issue/comment/edge surfaces;
  * live planner comment/edge enrichment regresses or is disabled;
  * a manager-planner decision demonstrably changes when a session transcript decision is provided only as data.
* The retest follows the SYMPH-962 Rev 2 Phase-A methodology, including Step P first, seed/discovery separation, live runtime planner parity, and transcript fencing.
* The retest records D, T, F, F*, per-session provenance, and a BUILD / NO-BUILD / REDIRECT verdict on SYMPH-962 or its successor.

## Verification

Before starting work, cite the observed trigger evidence and the relevant session or planner run. On completion, verify the same stop-gate and ratification flow used on 2026-06-29.

## Source refs

* SYMPH-962 final Phase-A verdict comment, 2026-06-29.
* SYMPH-972 Phase-A gate issue.
* Linear Doc `8c034c1269d2`.
* `docs/plans/2026-06-29-symph-962-phase-a-gate-spec.md`.

comments.body:
SYMPH-962 was **cancelled** (2026-06-29). Its post-hoc operator-session-mining approach is exactly the NO-BUILD this trigger records; the direction pivoted to **SYMPH-980** (decision-time capture inside dispatched *implement* sessions → a `## Closeout` comment) — a different approach and surface.

This trigger stands **unchanged and independent**: it tracks whether **operator-session transcript-only decisions** ever gain marginal planner value (the "operator-session capture" element parked in SYMPH-962's closeout). If a trigger condition is observed, re-run Phase-A per the 962 Rev 2 methodology and record the verdict here (or on a successor). issues.title: Spike: evaluate local-LLM claim/structure extractor for planner grounding (>=25 real examples)
issues.description:
Calibration spike (run in a separate agent) for the **central** local-LLM extractor in SYMPH-1017's planner grounding. This spike does **not** gate whether the extractor ships — the extractor is committed and central, with deterministic verification as its backstop. The spike tunes it: fixes the extractor's job, measures recall + false-positive rate on real data, and sets the operating thresholds it must meet (iterate the prompt/model to reach them, don't drop the extractor).

## Why

SYMPH-1017 wires a central local-LLM extractor into the planner: it maps prose (ticket bodies, comments, referenced/attached plan docs) into checkable claims + a decision-bearing digest + a plan's unit→claim/wave structure (for per-unit completion). Every extracted claim is backstopped by deterministic verification against a repo checkout. The open questions are not *whether* to build it but *how well it performs and where its thresholds sit* — which needs real data. Operator note (2026-07-01): referenced plans (e.g. the operator-supervisor plan) sequence multi-unit work in waves spanning PR boundaries; capturing per-unit completion is exactly the extractor's job, and this spike confirms it does so reliably.

## Acceptance criteria

* AC1: The extractor's job is specified before the spike runs — which of: prose→claim extraction, plan unit→claim/wave-structure mapping, the decision-bearing digest, and LLM comment-relevance scoring (SYMPH-1017 U10).
* AC2: A labeled eval set of ≥25 real examples drawn from actual Symphony tickets + their referenced/attached plan docs, including ≥1 multi-unit wave-spanning plan (e.g. operator-supervisor) and ≥1 ticket with a high-value agent-authored closeout comment. Each carries ground truth: checkable claims, per-unit completion state, and the expected already-done / superseded / not-done verdict.
* AC3: Measures the extractor's **recall** (share of real already-done/superseded cases caught) and its lift over the deterministic citation-only baseline (SYMPH-1017's Phase-A backstop). Reported as calibration data, not a build/no-build gate.
* AC4: Measures the **false-positive rate** — candidates wrongly concluded already-done when the named unit exists only as a stub/partial (SYMPH-1017 finding #4). Two-sided: real catches AND false culls.
* AC5: **Sets the operating thresholds** the extractor must meet (min recall / max false-positive), and the keep/drop relevance bar for comment-relevance (U10). Below threshold → iterate the prompt/model, not drop the extractor.
* AC6: Runs in a separate agent, report-only; no wiring into the live planner path.

## Source refs

* SYMPH-1017 design brief: docs/plans/2026-07-01-symph-1017-planner-deep-code-grounding-plan.md (Phase C = central extractor U9 + comment relevance U10)
* ce-doc-review 2026-07-01 findings #3/#4; operator correction 2026-07-01 — the LLM extractor is central, not contingent: this spike calibrates it, it does not gate it.

## Problem

PR #704 adds `DOC_EXTRACTION_CACHE`, a module-global content-hash cache for doc-following extraction results. issues.title: manager-plan CLI --persist fails cold: defaults to unstaged crabrunner version "dev"
issues.description:
## Problem

`symphony-manager-plan --persist` (which triggers the tier-1/tier-2 decorrelated review) invokes the crabrunner planner + review lanes with `SYMPHONY_CRABRUNNER_VERSION` **defaulting to** `dev` (`src/stage-execution/crabrunner-scheduler-client.ts:298-299`). The `dev` version is only pre-staged for the Crucible **controller** repo, not for symphony targets, so `crabrunner submit` fails:

```
crabrunner submit exited with code 1: crabrunner: staged crabrunner is missing for version dev
```

→ planner returns exit 3 (`Planner unavailable`), and the review never runs. The **live orchestrator** submits against a rollout version (e.g. `rollout-20260706T114021.621Z`), but the **standalone CLI lacks that version resolution** — an operator running `--persist` cold hits exit 3 with no hint that a version/root env is required.

## Repro

```bash
# cold: defaults to SYMPHONY_CRABRUNNER_ROOT unset / version "dev"
SYMPHONY_CRABRUNNER_ROOT=~/projects/crucible \
  symphony-manager-plan --project 9c1064215e8d --state Backlog --planner-grounding --persist
# → exit 3: "staged crabrunner is missing for version dev"
```

## Working config (the manual workaround)

```bash
SYMPHONY_CRABRUNNER_ROOT=~/.local/share/crucible/controller \
SYMPHONY_CRABRUNNER_VERSION=rollout-20260706T114021.621Z \
  symphony-manager-plan --project 9c1064215e8d --state Backlog --planner-grounding --persist
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `symphony-manager-plan --persist` works **cold** (no operator env spelunking): the CLI or its wrapper (`scripts/symphony-manager-plan`) resolves the current staged rollout version by default — the same one the live orchestrator uses — instead of literal `dev`.
- [ ] If no staged version is resolvable, fail with a **clear actionable error** naming `SYMPHONY_CRABRUNNER_ROOT` / `SYMPHONY_CRABRUNNER_VERSION` and how to find the current rollout, not a bare `staged crabrunner is missing for version dev`.
- [ ] `docs/operations/02-symphony-manager-plan.md` documents the crabrunner root/version requirement for `--persist` (today it is silent on both).

## Source refs

* `src/stage-execution/crabrunner-scheduler-client.ts:298-299` (`?? "dev"` default)
* `src/claude-runner/crabrunner-claude-runner.ts:113` (`SYMPHONY_CRABRUNNER_ROOT` required)
* Dogfood evidence: `docs/plans/2026-07-02-manager-plan-dogfood-runbook.md` → "Differential-review data point — 2026-07-06" (three attempts: version-default was the blocker).

## Notes

Surfaced while running the [SYMPH-1034](https://linear.app/mobilyze-llc/issue/SYMPH-1034/deferred-plan-review-trust-ramp-report-only-advisory-gate-symph-875) differential-review data point. **Substrate-adjacent** — if the operator prefers, fold into the pending crabrunner/substrate refactor rather than fixing standalone. The 2026-07-09 audit's manual clustering pass (192 open SYMPH issues → ~15 root-cause clusters, ~30 dispositions) is exactly the work that must become a standing process — and progressively hand off to the automated triage/planner as its judgment earns trust.

## Design principle

Separate **filing** (cheap, in-the-moment, provenance-rich — keep it) from **diagnosis** (batch, cross-ticket, code-verified — the triage layer). In-run filings land in Triage (auto-intake) and never drive dispatch directly; only the triage layer promotes to Backlog (planner candidate pool). The state semantics already encode this — the ramp formalizes the Triage→Backlog promotion gate and who operates it.

## The ramp (each phase gated on observed evidence, thresholds set from data — never guessed)

- [ ] **T0 — operator-led cadence (start now):** recurring root-cause triage pass (weekly, or per ~25 intake tickets) using the audit's rubric: read every comment, verify claims against fresh origin/main, cluster to root cause, disposition ∈ {keep, absorb, supersede, cancel-fixed, cancel-stale, needs-root-trace}, apply with comment trails. Rubric committed as a doc; each pass appends a dated disposition log (filesystem-first).
- [ ] **T1 — planner shadows triage:** the queue-triage/backlog-audit machinery emits proposed dispositions with root-cause tags for the same intake, report-only; agreement vs operator dispositions is scored per class (absorb / cancel / keep / root-promote). Prereqs: SYMPH-989 decision (cull candidates must be visible to the planner in proposal mode), SYMPH-965 + MOB-604 (attribution/relay so provenance is machine-readable), measurement window open (W0).
- [ ] **T2 — scoped autonomy:** auto-apply low-risk classes (exact-duplicate absorb; verified-fixed cancel with PR citation) with audit-not-gate digests (applied + logged + Slack digest, reversible); root-cause promotion (new root-fix ticket superseding N symptoms) stays advisory.
- [ ] **T3 — full authority:** planner owns Triage→Backlog dispositions inside its tick; operator reads digests. Final gate: reopen/rework rate on its dispositions and survival rate of its root-fix tickets through review.

## Standing invariants (all phases)

* "No promotion of harden-X band-aids without a root trace" is enforced at the TRIAGE layer, not the filing layer — filing stays cheap.
* Every disposition carries evidence (PR/commit citation for cancels; code refs for keeps) and a comment trail on the ticket.
* Intake volume resumes when dispatch restarts (post-SYMPH-949): T0 cadence must be running BEFORE that restart or the queue re-silts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage rubric doc committed (derived from the 2026-07-09 audit's clustering prompts) + first recurring T0 pass completed and logged
- [ ] T1 shadow-disposition records flowing with an agreement metric defined and measured over ≥2 cycles
- [ ] Written promotion criteria per phase, derived from T1's observed agreement — recorded on this issue before any T2 flip

Source: `docs/plans/2026-07-09-operational-readiness-audit.md` §C (intake-triage stream); operator directive 2026-07-09. Relates: SYMPH-989, SYMPH-965, SYMPH-1013, MOB-604.
